questions.text: एक एकबीजपत्री बीज (दाने) की अनुप्रस्थ-काट का आरेख नीचे दिया गया है, जिसके भाग-I, II तथा III को नामांकित किया गया है। उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसमें I, II तथा III भागों को सही अनुक्रम में दर्शाया गया है।
questions.text_english: Given below is a diagram of T.S. of a monocot seed with parts I, II & III labelled. Choose the option where parts I, II and III are identified correctly.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Pericarp, Endosperm, Coleorhiza. In a monocot seed (grain such as maize), the outermost layer I is the pericarp (fruit wall fused with seed coat), the large central food-storing region II is the endosperm, and the root-cap-like sheath at the bottom III is the coleorhiza. Option A is wrong because Part III is Coleorhiza, not Scutellum. Options C and D have incorrect assignments of all three parts.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) फलभित्ति, भ्रूणपोष, मूलांकुरचोल है। एकबीजपत्री बीज में बाहरी परत I फलभित्ति है, बड़ा केंद्रीय भाग II भ्रूणपोष है तथा निचला आवरण III मूलांकुरचोल है।

questions.text: मानव की द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिका में उपस्थित अलिंगी गुणसूत्रों की संख्या है
questions.text_english: The number of autosomes present in a human secondary spermatocyte
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 22. A human secondary spermatocyte is formed after the first meiotic division (Meiosis I), which is a reductive division. The primary spermatocyte (2n = 46) divides to give two secondary spermatocytes, each with the haploid number of 23 chromosomes total — 22 autosomes and 1 sex chromosome. Therefore the number of autosomes is 22. Option A (44) is the autosome count in a diploid cell, Option C (23) is the total chromosome number in the secondary spermatocyte, and Option D (46) is the diploid number.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 22 है। द्वितीयक शुक्राणु कोशिका अर्धसूत्री विभाजन-I के बाद बनती है और इसमें कुल 23 गुणसूत्र होते हैं जिनमें 22 अलिंगी गुणसूत्र होते हैं।

questions.text: एक बच्चे का रुधिर वर्ग-A है; उसके पिता का रुधिर वर्ग-B तथा माता का रुधिर वर्ग AB है। उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसमें पिता, माँ (माता) तथा बच्चे के जीनप्ररूप को सही क्रम में दिया गया है।
questions.text_english: A child with blood group A has father with blood group B and the mother with blood group AB. Choose the option that gives the correct genotypes of father, mother and the child.

options.A: पिता: I^A i, माता: I^B i, बच्चा: I^A i
options.B: पिता: I^A I^B, माता: I^A i, बच्चा: I^A I^A
options.C: पिता: I^B i, माता: I^A I^B, बच्चा: I^A i
options.D: पिता: I^B I^B, माता: I^A I^B, बच्चा: I^A I^A

options_english.A: Father: I^A i, Mother: I^B i, Child: I^A i
options_english.B: Father: I^A I^B, Mother: I^A i, Child: I^A I^A
options_english.C: Father: I^B i, Mother: I^A I^B, Child: I^A i
options_english.D: Father: I^B I^B, Mother: I^A I^B, Child: I^A I^A

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): Father I^B i, Mother I^A I^B, Child I^A i. The mother has blood group AB, so her genotype must be I^A I^B. The father has blood group B; his genotype can be I^B I^B or I^B i. The child has blood group A with genotype I^A i, meaning the child received I^A from the mother and i from the father — so the father must be I^B i. This is consistent only with option C. Options A and B give incorrect genotypes for the mother (blood group AB must be I^A I^B, not I^B i or I^A i). Option D cannot produce a child with genotype I^A i because I^B I^B father contributes no i allele.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। माता का रुधिर वर्ग AB है इसलिए उसका जीनप्ररूप I^A I^B है। पिता का रुधिर वर्ग B है तथा बच्चे को i एलील देने के लिए उसका जीनप्ररूप I^B i होना चाहिए। बच्चे का जीनप्ररूप I^A i (रुधिर वर्ग A) है।

questions.text: एक वंशावली विश्लेषण चार्ट में '○═□' निरूपित करता है
questions.text_english: In a pedigree chart '○═□' represents
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) mating between relatives (consanguineous mating). In a pedigree chart, a double horizontal line (═) connecting a circle (female) and a square (male) specifically indicates consanguineous mating, i.e., mating between closely related individuals. A single horizontal line represents unrelated mating (Option A). Affected individuals are shown by filled/shaded symbols (Option B). Non-identical twins are shown by diverging lines from a single point (Option D).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) रिश्तेदारों के बीच मैथुन (समरक्त मैथुन) है। वंशावली विश्लेषण चार्ट में दोहरी क्षैतिज रेखा (═) समरक्त मैथुन को दर्शाती है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प दिए गए पौधों के विकास का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाता है? (i) फर्न (ii) जिन्को (iii) जोस्टेरोफिलम (iv) नीटेल्स
questions.text_english: Which one of the following options shows the correct evolutionary order of the plants mentioned below? (i) Ferns (ii) Ginkgo (iii) Zosterophyllum (iv) Gnetales
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zosterophyllum → Ferns → Ginkgo → Gnetales. Zosterophyllum is one of the earliest vascular plants from the Silurian/Devonian period. Ferns (Pteridophytes) evolved next. Ginkgo belongs to Gymnosperms which came after ferns. Gnetales are the most advanced gymnosperms, considered closest to angiosperms, and appeared latest among the four. This makes the correct evolutionary sequence (iii), (i), (ii), (iv).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। विकासीय अनुक्रम है: जोस्टेरोफिलम → फर्न → जिन्को → नीटेल्स।

questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइडों के बीच फॉस्फोएस्टर बंध होता है
questions.text_english: The phosphoester linkage in the nucleotides is between

options.A: फॉस्फेट समूह तथा न्यूक्लियोसाइड के 3'C के 'OH' के बीच
options.B: फॉस्फेट समूह तथा न्यूक्लियोसाइड के 5'C के 'OH' के बीच
options.C: फॉस्फेट समूह तथा न्यूक्लियोसाइड के 3'C के 'H' के बीच
options.D: फॉस्फेट समूह तथा न्यूक्लियोसाइड के 5'C के 'H' के बीच

options_english.A: phosphate group and OH of 3'C of a nucleoside.
options_english.B: phosphate group and OH of 5'C of a nucleoside.
options_english.C: phosphate group and H of 3'C of a nucleoside.
options_english.D: phosphate group and H of 5'C of a nucleoside.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) phosphate group and OH of 5'C of a nucleoside. A nucleotide is formed when the phosphate group forms an ester bond with the hydroxyl (-OH) group at the 5' carbon of the sugar (deoxyribose or ribose) of a nucleoside. This is the phosphoester linkage. Options C and D are incorrect because the bond involves -OH, not -H. Option A is wrong because the linkage in a nucleotide formation is at the 5'C, not 3'C (the 3'OH is free and is used in phosphodiester bond formation in the polynucleotide chain).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। फॉस्फोएस्टर बंध, फॉस्फेट समूह तथा न्यूक्लियोसाइड के 5'C के -OH के बीच बनता है।

questions.text: सुकेन्द्री अनुलेखन के दौरान बनने वाले विषमांगी आरएनए को निम्न प्रकार से आरेखित किया गया है। विषमांगी केन्द्रीय आरएनए (hnRNA) में उपस्थित इंट्रॉनों तथा एक्जॉनों की संख्या क्रमश: है
questions.text_english: Given below is a heterogeneous RNA formed during Eukaryotic transcription. How many introns and exons respectively are present in the hnRNA?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 7 introns and 8 exons. In a hnRNA molecule, exons and introns alternate. If there are 8 exons, the introns between them will be 7 (since introns sit between exons). From the diagram shown, counting the looped segments (introns) gives 7 and the straight/wavy segments (exons) gives 8. The general rule is: if there are n exons, there are (n-1) introns. Hence 8 exons and 7 introns, making option D correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 7 इंट्रॉन और 8 एक्जॉन है। यदि n एक्जॉन हैं तो (n-1) इंट्रॉन होते हैं। आरेख में 8 एक्जॉन तथा 7 इंट्रॉन हैं।

questions.text: कॉलम-I तथा कॉलम-II में दी गई मदों का अध्ययन कीजिए। कॉलम-I की मदों का कॉलम-II की मदों के साथ सही मिलान वाले विकल्प को चुनिए। कॉलम-I: (a) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-I (b) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-II (c) आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-III। कॉलम-II: (i) 18s आरआरएनए (rRNA) (ii) एसएन आरएनएज (SnRNAs) (iii) hn आरएनए (hnRNA)
questions.text_english: Study the items of Column-I and those of Column-II. Choose the option that correctly matches the items of Column-I with those of Column-II. Column-I: (a) RNA polymerase I (b) RNA polymerase II (c) RNA polymerase III. Column-II: (i) 18s rRNA (ii) SnRNAs (iii) hnRNA
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): RNA polymerase I → 18s rRNA, RNA polymerase II → hnRNA, RNA polymerase III → SnRNAs. In eukaryotes, RNA Polymerase I transcribes rRNA genes including 18s rRNA. RNA Polymerase II transcribes the protein-coding genes to produce hnRNA (precursor of mRNA). RNA Polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and small nuclear RNAs (SnRNAs). Option A is incorrect because it assigns SnRNAs to RNA Pol II. Options B and C have wrong assignments for RNA Pol I and II.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-I → 18s rRNA, आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-II → hnRNA, आरएनए पॉलीमरेज-III → SnRNAs।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस सूक्ष्मजीव का उपयोग सिट्रिक अम्ल के व्यावसायिक तथा औद्योगिक उत्पादन में किया जाता है?
questions.text_english: For commercial and industrial production of citric acid, which one of the following microbes is used?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Aspergillus niger. This fungus is widely used for the commercial and industrial production of citric acid through fermentation. Lactobacillus sp. is used for lactic acid production. Clostridium butylicum is used for production of butyric acid and acetone. Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used in brewing and baking (ethanol production). Therefore, Aspergillus niger is the correct microbe for citric acid production.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) एस्पर्जिलस नाइजर है। इस कवक का उपयोग सिट्रिक अम्ल के व्यावसायिक उत्पादन में किया जाता है।

questions.text: यदि मेसेलसन तथा स्टाल के प्रयोग को 80 मिनट तक (तीसरी पीढ़ी) जारी रखा जाए तो संवर्धन में N15/N15 : N15/N14 : N14/N14 युक्त डीएनए का अनुपात क्या होगा?
questions.text_english: If Meselson and Stahl's experiment is continued for 80 minutes (till III generation) then what would be the ratio of DNA containing N15/N15 : N15/N14 : N14/N14 in the medium?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 0 : 1 : 3. In Meselson and Stahl's experiment, bacteria initially have N15/N15 DNA. After the first generation in N14 medium, all DNA is N15/N14 (hybrid). After the second generation, there are 2 hybrid (N15/N14) and 2 light (N14/N14) DNA molecules. After the third generation (80 minutes), we get 8 DNA molecules in total: 2 are hybrid (N15/N14) and 6 are light (N14/N14), and none is heavy (N15/N15). So the ratio of N15/N15 : N15/N14 : N14/N14 = 0 : 2 : 6 = 0 : 1 : 3.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 0 : 1 : 3 है। तीसरी पीढ़ी में 8 डीएनए अणुओं में 0 भारी, 2 संकर तथा 6 हल्के होते हैं, अनुपात 0 : 1 : 3 है।

options.A: पॉलीमरेज एंजाइम लाभकारी (वांछित) जीन को संवाहक डीएनए के साथ जोड़ता है।
options.B: जेल इलेक्ट्रोफोरेसिस का उपयोग डीएनए खंड के प्रवर्धन (आवर्धन) में किया जाता है।
options.C: पीसीआर का उपयोग लाभकारी जीन के पृथक्करण तथा विलगन के लिए किया जाता है।
options.D: प्लाज्मिड डीएनए इसके साथ जुड़े हुए डीएनए के स्थानांतरण हेतु संवाहक का कार्य करता है।

options_english.A: The polymerase enzyme joins the gene of interest and the vector DNA.
options_english.B: Gel electrophoresis is used for amplification of a DNA segment.
options_english.C: PCR is used for isolation and separation of gene of interest.
options_english.D: Plasmid DNA acts as vector to transfer the piece of DNA attached to it.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Plasmid DNA acts as a vector to transfer the piece of DNA (gene of interest) attached to it into the host cell. Option A is wrong because it is DNA ligase (not polymerase) that joins the gene of interest to the vector DNA. Option B is wrong because gel electrophoresis is used for separation and visualization of DNA fragments, not amplification — PCR is used for amplification. Option C is wrong because PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is used for amplification of a specific DNA segment, not for isolation and separation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। प्लाज्मिड डीएनए, उससे जुड़े डीएनए के स्थानांतरण हेतु संवाहक का कार्य करता है।

questions.text: मानव रुधिर में टी-लसीकाणुओं की संख्या के ह्रास होने के परिणामस्वरूप होता है
questions.text_english: The decrease in the T-Lymphocytes count in human blood will finally result in
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) decrease in antibodies. T-lymphocytes (T-helper cells) play a crucial role in activating B-lymphocytes, which then differentiate into plasma cells that produce antibodies. A decrease in T-lymphocyte count impairs this activation, leading to reduced B-cell activity and consequently a decrease in antibody (immunoglobulin) production. This is precisely what happens in AIDS, where HIV destroys T-helper (CD4+) cells. Antigens are foreign substances and their levels are not directly controlled by T-lymphocyte count.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) प्रतिरक्षी (प्रतिपिंडों) का ह्रास है। टी-लसीकाणु, बी-लसीकाणुओं को सक्रिय करते हैं जो प्रतिरक्षी बनाते हैं। टी-लसीकाणुओं की कमी से प्रतिरक्षी उत्पादन घटेगा।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): पीत पिंड (कार्पस ल्यूटियम) प्रोजेस्टेरोन हॉर्मोन स्रवित करता है। कारण (R): प्रोजेस्टेरोन हॉर्मोन गर्भाशय के अंत:स्तर के अनुरक्षण (को बनाए रखने) के लिए आवश्यक है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Corpus luteum secretes the hormone, progesterone. Reason (R): Hormone Progesterone is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन – अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दिए गए हैं। उचित विकल्प चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Question numbers 13 to 16 consist of two statements — Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer selecting the appropriate option.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The corpus luteum, formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation, secretes progesterone. Progesterone is specifically responsible for maintaining the endometrial lining of the uterus, making it suitable for implantation and sustaining early pregnancy. Thus the Reason (R) directly and correctly explains why the corpus luteum secretes progesterone (A).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन तथा कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। पीत पिंड प्रोजेस्टेरोन स्रवित करता है जो गर्भाशय के अंत:स्तर के अनुरक्षण के लिए आवश्यक है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): इंग्लैंड में औद्योगीकरण के पश्चात् श्वेत पंखी शलभों की संख्या कम हो गई। कारण (R): इंग्लैंड के ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में औद्योगीकरण का प्रभाव अधिक देखा गया।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): The number of white winged moths decreased after industrialisation in England. Reason (R): Effects of industrialisation were more marked in rural areas of England.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): (A) is true, but (R) is false. The Assertion is correct — after industrialisation in England, the white-winged (peppered) moths decreased in number because industrial soot darkened the tree bark, making white moths more visible to predators (natural selection favoured dark/melanistic moths). However, the Reason is false — the effects of industrialisation were more marked in industrial/urban areas, not in rural areas. It was in industrial cities like Manchester that the dark moths thrived, not in clean rural regions where white moths continued to survive.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अभिकथन सही है परन्तु कारण गलत है। औद्योगीकरण का प्रभाव शहरी/औद्योगिक क्षेत्रों में अधिक था, ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में नहीं।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): स्ट्रेप्टोकोकस न्युमोनी तथा हीमोफिलस इंफ्लुएंजी मानव में संक्रामक रोगों के लिए उत्तरदायी हैं। कारण (R): एक संक्रमित व्यक्ति द्वारा विमुक्त (छोड़े गए) एयरोसॉल को साँस द्वारा अंदर लेने से स्वस्थ व्यक्ति को संक्रमण हो जाता है।

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): (A) is true, but (R) is false. The Assertion is correct — restriction endonucleases do recognise and cut specific palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA. However, the Reason is false. PstI and PvuI are not recognition sites within a single palindromic sequence; they are two different restriction enzymes that each recognise their own specific palindromic sequences. A palindromic sequence is one where the sequence on one strand read 5' to 3' is the same as the sequence on the complementary strand read 5' to 3'. Each restriction enzyme recognises one specific palindrome.

sub_questions.solution: Malarial symptoms do not appear immediately because after entry into the bloodstream, the sporozoites of Plasmodium first travel to the liver cells (hepatocytes) where they multiply and develop into merozoites through the exoerythrocytic cycle. sub_questions.solution: After the restriction enzyme cuts the palindromic sequence (AAGCTT), the DNA is cut between A and AGCTT on each strand, generating fragments with short single-stranded overhangs: one fragment ends in 5'-A and the other starts with 5'-AGCTT-3', leaving complementary single-stranded tails on each end.

sub_questions.text_english: Why are the ends generated after digestion called 'Sticky Ends'?

sub_questions.solution: The ends generated after restriction enzyme digestion are called sticky ends because they have short single-stranded overhanging sequences (tails) that are complementary to each other. These unpaired single-stranded portions can form hydrogen bonds (base-pair) with any complementary single-stranded sequence, allowing them to 'stick' or anneal together — which is essential for inserting the gene of interest into the vector during recombinant DNA technology.

sub_questions.text_english: A bilobed dithecous anther has 200 microspore mother cells per microsporangium. How many male gametophytes can be produced by this anther?

key_points: Dithecous anther: 2 thecae, each theca has 2 microsporangia = 4 microsporangia total
Each microsporangium has 200 MMC, each MMC produces 4 microspores by meiosis
Total pollen = 4 x 200 x 4 = 3200; each pollen = 1 male gametophyte, so 3200 male gametophytes

sub_questions.solution: A dithecous anther has two thecae, each theca contains two microsporangia, giving a total of 4 microsporangia per anther. Each microsporangium has 200 microspore mother cells (MMC). Each MMC undergoes meiosis to produce 4 microspores (pollen grains). Total microspores = 4 microsporangia x 200 MMC x 4 microspores = 3200 pollen grains. Each pollen grain develops into one male gametophyte. Therefore, 3200 male gametophytes will be produced by this anther.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the composition of intine and exine layers of a pollen grains.

key_points: Exine: made of sporopollenin — most resistant biological material known
Intine: made of cellulose and pectin

sub_questions.solution: A pollen grain has two wall layers. The outer layer is the exine, which is made of sporopollenin — one of the most chemically resistant biological substances known, capable of withstanding high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis. It has characteristic apertures called germ pores. The inner layer is the intine, which is thin and made of cellulose and pectin. The intine is continuous and forms the pollen tube during germination.

sub_questions.text_english: List two reasons that make copper releasing IUDs as effective contraceptives.

key_points: Copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
IUD makes uterus hostile to implantation / phagocytosis of sperm

sub_questions.solution: Copper-releasing IUDs (such as Cu-T) are effective contraceptives for two reasons: first, the copper ions released are toxic to sperm — they suppress sperm motility and reduce the fertilising capacity of sperms, preventing fertilisation. Second, the IUD creates a local inflammatory reaction in the uterus that makes the uterine environment hostile to implantation, and also promotes phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain how the intake of oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy in humans.

key_points: Oral pills contain synthetic estrogen and progesterone
They inhibit ovulation by suppressing FSH and LH secretion
They also alter cervical mucus and endometrium making implantation difficult

sub_questions.solution: Oral contraceptive pills (such as Saheli or combined estrogen-progesterone pills) prevent pregnancy through several mechanisms. They contain synthetic hormones — estrogen and progesterone — which, when taken regularly, provide a sustained high level of these hormones in the blood. This suppresses the secretion of FSH and LH from the pituitary gland, thereby inhibiting the development of follicles and preventing ovulation. Additionally, they alter the consistency of cervical mucus, making it hostile to sperm penetration, and change the endometrial lining to prevent implantation even if fertilisation occurs.

questions.text_english: Using a Punnett square workout the distribution of an autosomal phenotypic feature in the first filial generation after a cross between a homozygous female and a heterozygous male for a single locus.

key_points: Homozygous female: AA (or aa) x Heterozygous male: Aa
If AA x Aa: all offspring Aa (heterozygous) — all show dominant phenotype (100%)
If aa x Aa: offspring 50% Aa (dominant) and 50% aa (recessive)

questions.solution: Let the homozygous dominant female be AA and the heterozygous male be Aa. The Punnett square cross is: Female gametes: A, A; Male gametes: A, a. The four possible combinations are: AA, Aa, AA, Aa — giving a genotypic ratio of 2 AA : 2 Aa = 1:1 (homozygous dominant : heterozygous). Since both AA and Aa show the dominant phenotype, the phenotypic ratio in F1 is 100% dominant : 0% recessive — all offspring will show the dominant trait. Alternatively, if the homozygous female is aa (recessive) crossed with Aa male: offspring are 1 Aa : 1 aa, giving a 1:1 phenotypic ratio (50% dominant : 50% recessive).

Assuming homozygous dominant female (AA) × heterozygous male (Aa): The Punnett square gives gametes A and A from female, and A and a from male. Combining them gives four offspring — AA, Aa, AA, Aa. The genotypic ratio is 2 AA : 2 Aa, and since both express the dominant phenotype, the phenotypic ratio is 4 dominant : 0 recessive, i.e., all F1 offspring show the dominant phenotype. If the question intends homozygous recessive female (aa) × Aa male, the Punnett square gives Aa, Aa, aa, aa — a 1:1 ratio, with 50% showing dominant and 50% showing recessive phenotype.

questions.text_english: How does the process of Natural Selection affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium? Explain with the help of graphs.

key_points: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium states allele frequencies remain constant unless disturbed
Natural selection changes allele frequencies by favouring adaptive traits
Graph shows three types: directional, stabilising, and disruptive selection

questions.solution: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium states that allele and genotype frequencies in a population remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of evolutionary forces. Natural selection is one of the key forces that disturbs this equilibrium. When natural selection operates, individuals with advantageous phenotypes survive and reproduce more successfully, increasing the frequency of their alleles in the population while reducing frequencies of less favourable alleles. In directional selection, the mean phenotype shifts towards one extreme (e.g., industrial melanism — dark moths increase). In stabilising selection, extreme phenotypes are eliminated and intermediate types are favoured. In disruptive selection, both extremes are favoured, leading to two distinct peaks. All three modes shift allele frequencies away from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, driving evolution.

sub_questions.text_english: The insulin synthesised in our body is different from that synthesised by Eli Lilly company using recombinant DNA technology. Differentiate between them.

key_points: Body insulin: synthesised as pre-pro-insulin, then pro-insulin, then active insulin (A and B chains connected by C-peptide which is removed)
Recombinant insulin (Humulin): A and B chains synthesised separately in E. coli, then combined; no C-peptide involved in the process

sub_questions.solution: Insulin synthesised in our body (by beta cells of pancreatic islets) is initially produced as pre-pro-insulin, which is converted to pro-insulin. Pro-insulin contains three chains (A, B, and C). The C-peptide is removed enzymatically to give the mature, active insulin consisting of A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds. In contrast, the recombinant insulin (Humulin) produced by Eli Lilly company is made by separately synthesising the A and B chains in E. coli bacteria using recombinant DNA technology. These chains are then extracted and combined in vitro by forming disulfide bonds, bypassing the pro-insulin stage entirely.

Recombinant human insulin is structurally identical to human insulin and does not trigger immune response

sub_questions.solution: Insulin extracted from animal sources (pig or cattle) is no longer in common use because it differs slightly in amino acid sequence from human insulin. When injected into some diabetic patients, this minor structural difference is recognised as foreign by the immune system, triggering allergic reactions and immunological complications. Recombinant human insulin (produced using human insulin gene in bacteria) is structurally identical to human insulin and is therefore safer, more effective, and does not provoke immune reactions.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw a graph for a population whose population density has reached the carrying capacity.

key_points: S-shaped (logistic) growth curve where population plateaus at carrying capacity K

sub_questions.solution: The graph for a population that has reached carrying capacity is a logistic (S-shaped or sigmoid) growth curve. On this graph, the x-axis shows time and the y-axis shows population size (N). The curve rises slowly initially (lag phase), then accelerates (exponential phase), and finally levels off horizontally at a value K (the carrying capacity), showing that the population has stabilised and is no longer growing.

sub_questions.text: दो समष्टि वृद्धि वक्रों में से कौन सा वृद्धि वक्र अधिकतर समष्टियों के लिए अधिक यथार्थ-पूर्ण माना जाता है? क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of the two population growth curves, which one is considered a more realistic for most populations? Why?

key_points: Logistic (S-shaped) growth curve is more realistic
Because in nature resources are always limited, so populations cannot grow indefinitely

sub_questions.solution: The logistic (S-shaped) growth curve is considered more realistic for most populations. This is because in nature, food, space, water, and other resources are always limited. As population density increases, competition for resources intensifies, birth rates decline and death rates increase, eventually limiting further growth. No population can grow exponentially (J-shaped) indefinitely because it would exceed the carrying capacity of its habitat. The logistic model incorporates these limiting factors and accurately reflects real population dynamics.

Equation: dN/dt = rN (where r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, N = population size)

sub_questions.solution: When resources are unlimited, the population shows exponential (J-shaped) growth. The growth curve is a J-shaped curve where population size increases continuously and steeply with time without any plateau. The equation for this growth is dN/dt = rN, where dN/dt is the rate of change of population size, N is the current population size, and r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase. This model assumes unlimited resources, no competition, and ideal environmental conditions.

questions.text: हमारे शरीर में प्रतिरक्षा दो प्रकार की होती है : (i) सहज प्रतिरक्षा तथा (ii) उपार्जित प्रतिरक्षा। सहज प्रतिरक्षा एक प्रकार का अविशिष्ट रक्षा उपागम है, जबकि उपार्जित प्रतिरक्षा रोगजनक-विशिष्ट है; जिसे विशिष्ट प्रतिरक्षा भी कहा जाता है जिसका अभिलक्षण स्मृति है। प्रतिरक्षी अणु किसी प्रतिजन के प्रति विशिष्ट होते हैं। हमारे शरीर में विभिन्न प्रकार के प्रतिरक्षी अणु निर्मित होते हैं; इनके चार उदाहरण IgA, IgE, IgG तथा IgM हैं। जब हमारा शरीर किसी रोगजनक से पहली बार सामना करता है तो इसे प्राथमिक अनुक्रिया कहते हैं तथा जब पुन: उसी प्रतिजन/रोगजनक से उसका सामना होता है तो उसे द्वितीयक अनुक्रिया कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Immunity in our body is of two types: (i) Innate immunity and (ii) acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas acquired immunity is pathogen-specific; it is called specific immunity too. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are different types of antibodies produced in our body: they are IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response when it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same Antigen/Pathogen.

sub_questions.text: दो प्रकार की विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं के नाम लिखिए जो प्राथमिक तथा द्वितीयक प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया को सम्पादित करती हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the two types of specialised cells which carry out the primary and secondary immune response.

key_points: B-lymphocytes (B cells) — produce antibodies
T-lymphocytes (T cells) — cell-mediated immunity

sub_questions.solution: The two types of specialised cells are B-lymphocytes (B cells) and T-lymphocytes (T cells). B-lymphocytes mediate humoral immunity by differentiating into plasma cells that secrete antibodies during the primary response, and into memory B cells that enable the faster and stronger secondary response. T-lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity and also help activate B cells through T-helper cells.

sub_questions.text: प्रतिरक्षी अणु – माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा को तरल प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया (ह्युमोरल इम्यून रेसपांस) भी कहा जाता है, क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the antibody-mediated immunity also called as humoral immune response?

key_points: Antibodies circulate in blood and lymph (body fluids/humors), hence called humoral

sub_questions.solution: Antibody-mediated immunity is called humoral immune response because the antibodies produced by plasma cells (derived from B-lymphocytes) are secreted into the blood and lymph — the body fluids historically called 'humors'. Since the immunity is carried out through these circulating body fluids (blood and lymph) rather than through direct cell-to-cell contact, it is termed humoral (from the Latin word 'humor' meaning body fluid).

sub_questions.text: यदि समुचित (उपयुक्त) दाता से प्रतिरोपण अंग न प्राप्त किया जाए तो प्रतिरोपण सामान्यत: अस्वीकार (नकार) कर दिए जाते हैं। (i) प्रतिरोप को अस्वीकार करने के लिए हमारे शरीर के प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र में पाये जाने वाले विशिष्ट अभिलक्षण का उल्लेख कीजिए। (ii) इसमें शामिल कोशिकाओं तथा प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया के प्रकार का नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The organ transplants are often rejected if not taken from suitable compatible persons. (i) Mention the characteristic of our immune system that is responsible for the graft rejection. (ii) Name the type of immune response and the cell involved in it.

key_points: Immune characteristic: ability to distinguish self from non-self (MHC/HLA specificity)
Cell involved: T-lymphocytes (cytotoxic T cells); Type: Cell-mediated immune response

sub_questions.solution: The characteristic of the immune system responsible for graft rejection is its ability to distinguish 'self' from 'non-self' based on the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) — also called HLA (Human Leukocyte Antigens) in humans. When a transplanted organ has different MHC antigens than the host, the immune system recognises it as foreign and mounts a rejection response. The type of immune response involved is cell-mediated immune response (CMI), and the cells responsible are cytotoxic T-lymphocytes (T-killer cells/CD8+ cells), which directly attack and destroy the transplanted tissue.

sub_questions.text: सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा से किस प्रकार भिन्न है?
sub_questions.text_english: How is active immunity different from passive immunity?

key_points: Active: body produces its own antibodies in response to antigen; has memory; slow but long-lasting
Passive: ready-made antibodies injected from outside; no memory; fast but short-lived

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity is the type of immunity in which the host body itself produces antibodies in response to exposure to an antigen (either through infection or vaccination). It has immunological memory, develops slowly, but provides long-lasting protection. Passive immunity, on the other hand, involves the administration of ready-made antibodies (preformed antibodies) produced in another individual or animal into the patient's body — for example, anti-tetanus serum or anti-snake venom. Passive immunity provides immediate protection but is short-lived because there is no memory and the antibodies are gradually degraded.

sub_questions.text_english: Name the main enzyme involved in the process of transcription.

key_points: RNA polymerase

sub_questions.solution: The main enzyme involved in the process of transcription is RNA polymerase. In prokaryotes, a single RNA polymerase performs all transcription. In eukaryotes, RNA Polymerase II is primarily responsible for transcribing protein-coding genes (mRNA precursors).

sub_questions.text_english: Identify coding strand and template strand of DNA in the transcription unit.

key_points: Coding strand: the strand running 3' to 5' in the diagram (top strand, same sequence as mRNA with T instead of U)
Template strand: the strand running 5' to 3' in the diagram (bottom strand), read by RNA polymerase

sub_questions.solution: In the transcription unit diagram, the strand running 3' to 5' direction (from which RNA polymerase reads and synthesises RNA in the 5' to 3' direction) is the template strand (also called antisense strand). The other strand, which runs 5' to 3' and has the same sequence as the RNA produced (except T instead of U), is the coding strand (also called the sense strand or non-template strand). From the given diagram, the strand with 3' end on the left side is the template strand, and the one with 5' end on the left is the coding strand.

sub_questions.text: चित्र में (C) तथा (D) को पहचानिए तथा अनुलेखन प्रक्रम में उनकी सार्थकता (महत्व) का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify (C) and (D) in the diagram, mention their significance in the process of transcription.

key_points: C = Promoter region; significance: RNA polymerase binds here to initiate transcription
D = Terminator region; significance: signals the end of transcription and RNA polymerase detaches

sub_questions.solution: In the transcription unit diagram, C represents the Promoter and D represents the Terminator. The promoter (C) is a specific DNA sequence located upstream (5' end) of the gene where RNA polymerase binds to initiate the process of transcription. It determines which strand is used as template and controls the frequency of transcription. The terminator (D) is a specific DNA sequence at the 3' end of the transcription unit that signals the end of transcription. When RNA polymerase reaches the terminator, the newly synthesised RNA molecule is released and the enzyme detaches from the DNA.

sub_questions.text: अनुलेखन एकल (इकाई) में (C) तथा (D) की अवस्थिति का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe the location of (C) and (D) in the transcription unit.

key_points: C (Promoter): located upstream (5' end/3' end of template strand) of the structural gene
D (Terminator): located downstream (3' end/5' end of template strand) at the end of the structural gene

sub_questions.solution: In a transcription unit, C (the Promoter) is located upstream of the structural gene — it is present at the 5' end of the coding strand (which corresponds to the 3' end of the template strand). It lies just before the start site of transcription. D (the Terminator) is located downstream of the structural gene — it is present at the 3' end of the coding strand (5' end of template strand), marking the end of the region to be transcribed. The structural gene (the region actually transcribed) lies between the promoter (C) and the terminator (D).

sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Describe the process of megasporogenesis in an angiosperm. (ii) Draw a diagram of a mature embryo sac of an angiosperm. Label its any four parts.

key_points: Megasporogenesis: diploid megaspore mother cell (MMC) in nucellus undergoes meiosis to produce 4 haploid megaspores
Three of the four megaspores degenerate; only one functional megaspore survives (usually chalazal end)
Functional megaspore undergoes 3 mitotic divisions to form 8-nucleate embryo sac (Polygonum type)
Embryo sac parts: egg cell, 2 synergids, central cell with 2 polar nuclei, 3 antipodal cells

sub_questions.solution: Megasporogenesis is the process of formation of megaspores from the megaspore mother cell (MMC). In an angiosperm, the nucellus of the ovule contains a diploid megaspore mother cell (MMC or megasporocyte). The MMC undergoes meiosis (meiotic division) to produce four haploid megaspores arranged in a linear tetrad. Out of the four megaspores, three (usually the three micropylar ones) degenerate, and only one functional megaspore survives, typically at the chalazal end. This functional megaspore is the first cell of the female gametophyte. It enlarges and undergoes three successive mitotic divisions — first division gives 2 nuclei, second gives 4 nuclei (moving to opposite poles), and the third gives 8 nuclei in total (4 at each pole). The nuclei then organise into cells: at the micropylar end, 3 nuclei form the egg apparatus (1 egg cell + 2 synergids); at the chalazal end, 3 nuclei form the antipodal cells; and one nucleus from each pole migrates to the centre to form the 2 polar nuclei within the large central cell. This mature 7-celled, 8-nucleate structure is the embryo sac (female gametophyte). For the diagram: The mature embryo sac should be drawn showing — 1. Egg cell (at micropylar end), 2. Two synergids (flanking the egg cell), 3. Central cell with two polar nuclei, 4. Three antipodal cells (at chalazal end).

sub_questions.text: (B) मादा प्राइमेट स्तनधारियों में होने वाले जनन चक्र को आर्त्तव चक्र (मेन्स्टूअल साइकिल) कहते हैं। आर्त्तव चक्र की शुरुआत यौवनारंभ से होती है। अग्रगामी प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए। (i) आर्त्तव चक्र की चार प्रावस्थाओं को सही अनुक्रम में लिखिए। (ii) आर्त्तव चक्र में ऋतुस्राव (रजोधर्म) कितनी अवधि तक जारी रहता है? sub_questions.text_english: (B) The reproductive cycle in the female primates is called menstrual cycle. The first menstruation begins at puberty. Answer the following questions: (i) Name the four phases of menstrual cycle in a proper sequence. (ii) How long does the menstrual phase last in a menstrual cycle? (iii) When and why hormones estrogen and progesterone reach their peak levels respectively, in the menstrual cycle? (iv) Give the significance of LH surge.

key_points: Four phases: Menstrual phase → Follicular phase → Ovulatory phase → Luteal phase
Menstrual phase lasts 3-5 days
Estrogen peaks during late follicular phase (day 12-13) due to growing Graafian follicle; Progesterone peaks during luteal phase (days 16-24) due to corpus luteum
LH surge causes ovulation (release of mature ovum from Graafian follicle)

sub_questions.solution: The menstrual cycle in female primates is approximately 28 days long and begins at puberty. The four phases in proper sequence are: Menstrual phase, Follicular phase (Proliferative phase), Ovulatory phase, and Luteal phase (Secretory phase). The menstrual phase lasts approximately 3 to 5 days, during which the endometrial lining breaks down and is shed along with blood due to a fall in progesterone and estrogen levels. Estrogen reaches its peak level during the late follicular phase (around days 12-13). It peaks at this time because the developing Graafian follicle secretes large amounts of estrogen, which also triggers the LH surge. Progesterone reaches its peak level during the luteal phase (approximately days 16-24). After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into the corpus luteum, which actively secretes progesterone to maintain and prepare the endometrium for potential implantation. The LH surge (a sudden, sharp rise in LH levels around day 14) is of great significance because it triggers ovulation — the release of the mature ovum (secondary oocyte) from the Graafian follicle — and also initiates the conversion of the ruptured follicle into the corpus luteum.

sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Explain how is a bacterial cell made 'competent' to take up recombinant DNA from the medium. (ii) Explain the steps of amplification of gene of interest using PCR technique.

key_points: Competence: treat bacterial cells with divalent cations (CaCl2) to increase permeability; heat shock at 42°C followed by ice incubation; electroporation as alternative method
PCR steps: Denaturation (94°C — DNA strands separate), Annealing (50-65°C — primers bind), Extension (72°C — Taq polymerase extends new strands)

sub_questions.solution: To make a bacterial cell competent to take up recombinant DNA, the cell membrane must be made more permeable. This is achieved by treating bacterial cells with divalent cation solutions such as calcium chloride (CaCl2). The CaCl2 treatment weakens the cell wall and membrane structure, allowing DNA molecules to enter more easily. The cells are then subjected to a brief heat shock (placed at 42°C for a short period and then immediately shifted to ice). This sudden temperature change creates transient pores in the membrane through which the recombinant DNA enters the cell. An alternative physical method is electroporation, where brief electric pulses are applied to create temporary pores in the membrane. PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) amplifies a specific DNA segment through three repeating steps: first, Denaturation — the double-stranded DNA template is heated to about 94°C, causing the hydrogen bonds to break and the two strands to separate; second, Annealing — the temperature is lowered to 50-65°C, allowing short synthetic oligonucleotide primers (complementary to the two ends of the target sequence) to bind to each strand; third, Extension — the temperature is raised to 72°C, at which the thermostable Taq DNA polymerase extends the primers by adding complementary nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction, synthesising new DNA strands. Each cycle doubles the number of copies of the target DNA, and after 30-35 cycles, millions of copies of the target gene are produced.

sub_questions.text: (B) (i) पारजीवी (ट्रांसजेनिक) जन्तु क्या हैं? (ii) इन जन्तुओं का निर्माण क्यों किया जाता है? किन्हीं चार कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) What are transgenic animals? (ii) Why are these animals being produced? Explain any four reasons.

key_points: Transgenic animals: animals with a foreign gene (transgene) stably integrated into their genome
Reason 1: To study gene function and regulation
Reason 2: Production of useful biological products (e.g., human proteins in milk)
Reason 3: Drug testing / safety evaluation
Reason 4: Disease models for study of human genetic diseases

sub_questions.solution: Transgenic animals are those animals whose genome has been altered by the stable introduction of a foreign gene (transgene) from another species, using recombinant DNA technology. The most commonly used transgenic animal is the mouse. These animals are produced for four major reasons: first, to study normal physiology and development — by introducing a specific gene or deleting it, scientists can study gene expression, function, and regulation under normal and pathological conditions; second, for production of valuable biological substances — transgenic animals (such as transgenic cattle) can be engineered to produce useful human proteins like alpha-1-antitrypsin or clotting factors in their milk, providing a cost-effective source for pharmaceutical use; third, for vaccine safety testing — transgenic mice are used to test the safety and efficacy of new vaccines before human trials; fourth, as disease models — transgenic animals can be engineered to carry genes for human diseases (e.g., Alzheimer's disease, cancer, diabetes), providing valuable models to study disease mechanisms and test potential treatments.

sub_questions.text_english: (A) (i) Explain giving three reasons why tropics show greatest levels of species diversity. (ii) Draw a graph showing species-area relationship. Name the naturalist who studied such relationship. Write the observation made by him.

key_points: Reason 1: Tropics have remained undisturbed for millions of years — longer evolutionary time
Reason 2: Tropical environments are less seasonal and more constant/predictable — more niche specialisation
Reason 3: More solar energy available — higher productivity supporting more species
Species-area relationship: Alexander von Humboldt; observation: species richness increases with increasing explored area up to a limit; log S = log C + Z log A

sub_questions.solution: Tropical regions show the greatest levels of species diversity for three main reasons: first, the tropics have remained climatically stable and undisturbed for millions of years (unlike temperate regions which were severely affected by glaciation), providing a much longer evolutionary time for speciation and diversification of species; second, tropical environments have a relatively constant, predictable climate with little seasonal variation, which allows greater ecological specialisation and niche differentiation — more species can coexist because resources are stable year-round; third, the tropics receive more solar energy throughout the year, supporting much higher primary productivity, which in turn provides food and habitat for a greater diversity and abundance of species at higher trophic levels. The species-area relationship was studied by the naturalist Alexander von Humboldt. He observed that within a region, species richness increases with increasing area up to a certain limit. This relationship, when plotted on a log scale, yields a straight line described by the equation: log S = log C + Z log A, where S is species richness, A is the area, Z is the slope (regression coefficient), and C is the y-intercept. The value of Z typically ranges from 0.1 to 0.2 for smaller regions.

sub_questions.text_english: (B) (i) The world is facing the accelerated rate of species extinctions due to human activities. Explain any three major causes of biodiversity losses. (ii) Describe 'Ex situ' approach for conserving biodiversity. Give any two examples.

key_points: Cause 1: Habitat loss and fragmentation (deforestation, urbanisation)
Cause 2: Over-exploitation (hunting, poaching, over-fishing)
Cause 3: Invasive alien species / Co-extinctions
Ex situ conservation: protecting threatened species outside natural habitat
Examples: Zoological parks (zoos), botanical gardens, seed banks, wildlife safari parks

sub_questions.solution: The three major causes of biodiversity loss due to human activities are: first, habitat loss and fragmentation — this is the most significant cause. Deforestation for agriculture, urbanisation, and industrialisation destroys natural habitats, eliminating species that cannot survive elsewhere. Fragmentation isolates populations and reduces genetic diversity, making them more vulnerable to extinction. Second, over-exploitation — many species are being harvested at rates faster than their natural populations can replenish. Examples include over-fishing of marine species, hunting of tigers and elephants for their body parts, and excessive collection of medicinal plants. Third, introduction of invasive alien species — when non-native species are introduced (deliberately or accidentally) into a new ecosystem, they can outcompete native species for resources, act as predators, or cause diseases, leading to the decline and extinction of native species (e.g., Nile perch introduced in Lake Victoria caused extinction of many native cichlid fish). Ex situ conservation refers to the conservation of threatened and endangered species outside their natural habitats. In this approach, animals and plants are maintained in controlled environments where they are given protection, proper care, and where breeding programmes can be conducted to increase their numbers. Two examples of ex situ conservation are: Zoological parks (zoos) and wildlife safari parks — where threatened animals are maintained and bred in captivity (e.g., breeding programmes for the white-backed vulture); and Botanical gardens and seed banks — where rare and endangered plant species are grown and their seeds are preserved at low temperatures (e.g., the Millennium Seed Bank in the UK and the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources in India).
